region: Central Africa (southern Cameroon, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, both Congos, CAR, southern Chad, Angola, western Zambia, northern Namibia fringe)

polities.name: Kingdom of Kongo
polities.note: Height c.1500-1665 from the Congo river to the Dande/Loje and east to the Kwango marches; battle of Mbwila 1665 began a civil war (1665-1709) that left provinces autonomous; restored by Pedro IV 1709 but much smaller and decentralised; Portuguese vassal/protectorate from 1857/1888; kingship ended 1914.

polities.name: Soyo
polities.note: Coastal province of Kongo at the Congo mouth; effectively independent from c.1641 under Count Daniel da Silva, defeated Portuguese at Kitombo 1670; remained autonomous until absorbed into Portuguese Angola in the 1880s.

polities.name: Mbata (Kongo province)
polities.note: Eastern Kongo province ruled by its own hereditary-elective dukes; acted independently during the civil war 1665-1709; later re-absorbed. Extent approximate (Inkisi to Kwango marches).

polities.name: Nsundi (Kongo province)
polities.note: Northern Kongo province between the lower Congo and the Inkisi, traditionally held by the heir; autonomous in the civil war. Extent approximate.

polities.name: Mbamba (Kongo province)
polities.note: Southwestern march of Kongo between the Mbridge and Loje rivers facing Portuguese Angola; Kimpanzu faction base during the civil war. Extent approximate.

polities.name: Kibangu (Kongo court in exile)
polities.note: Mountain stronghold from which rival Kongo kings ruled after Mbanza Kongo was abandoned (Manuel I overthrown 1688, Álvaro X to 1695, then Pedro IV); Pedro IV reoccupied São Salvador 1709 and his descendants kept Kibangu as princes after 1718.

polities.name: Kingdom of Loango
polities.note: Vili kingdom on the coast north of the Chiloango; separated from Kongo by c.1550; at height ruled from Mayumba to the Chiloango and inland to the Mayombe; French protectorate 1883.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kakongo
polities.note: Origins before the 13th c. per Wikipedia. Small coastal kingdom between Loango and Ngoyo (ports Malemba, Cabinda shore); claimed as tributary by Kongo; Portuguese protectorate by Treaty of Simulambuco 1885.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ngoyo
polities.note: Origins before the 13th c. per Wikipedia. Woyo kingdom around Cabinda bay north of the Congo mouth; Portuguese protectorate (Simulambuco) 1885; ruling Mambuku title survived to 20th c.

polities.name: Tio Kingdom
polities.note: Teke kingdom on the Batéké plateaux north and west of Pool Malebo; c.320 x 240 km; capital at Mbe (later moved to Ngõ mid-19th c.); Makoko Iloo's treaty with de Brazza 10 Sep 1879, French protectorate 1880.

polities.name: Mwene Muji
polities.note: Riverine kingdom of the lower Kasai with navy and trade dominance, around Lake Mai-Ndombe and south toward Idiofa, along the Kasai, Kwilu, Kamtsha, Lukenie; unity broke in the early 17th century (Boma broke away); remnant polity to c.1900. Extent highly uncertain.

polities.name: Boma Kingdom
polities.note: Broke from Mwene Muji in the early 17th c. and took its northern territories near Lake Mai-Ndombe and the lower Kwa; described as controlling fifteen 'kings' in the 1640s; close to Tio; ended under Congo Free State c.1900. Seat location approximate.

polities.name: Bolia Kingdom
polities.note: Sacred kingship (nkumu) east and northeast of Lake Mai-Ndombe; controlled the lake after defeating Bozanga; in 1767 reported as three subordinate territories under a Bolia king; Congo Free State from 1880s-1890s. Founding date disputed (12th to 18th c.).

polities.name: Kingdom of Ndongo
polities.note: Mbundu kingdom between the Lukala/Bengo and the Kwanza; tributary of Kongo until c.1556; Portuguese war from 1579 stripped the west; Njinga moved east to Matamba 1631; a Portuguese-backed vassal king held Pungo Andongo 1626-1671, extinguished 1671.

polities.name: Kingdom of Matamba
polities.note: Mbundu kingdom east of Ndongo along the upper Lukala to the Kwango; tributary to Kongo in the 16th c.; conquered by Njinga 1631 and made the base of Ndongo-Matamba; peace with Portugal 1656; Portuguese vassal from 1744; finally annexed 1909.

polities.name: Kasanje Kingdom
polities.note: Imbangala kingdom in the Baixa de Cassange on the middle Kwango; middleman between Lunda and Luanda slave trade; extinguished by Portugal 1912 (Portuguese occupation 1850s, revolts).

polities.name: Holo Kingdom
polities.note: Small Imbangala-influenced kingdom on the Kwango north of Kasanje (Kwango river crossing on the Lunda trade route); tributary to Lunda/Yaka sphere.

polities.name: Shinje
polities.note: Lunda-derived chiefdom east of the Kwango opposite Kasanje, controlling the trade route to Musumba; occupied by Chokwe expansion late 19th c.

polities.name: Kisama
polities.note: Loose group of salt-producing sobas south of the lower Kwanza that resisted Portugal and sheltered runaways for three centuries; conquered piecemeal in the 19th c.

polities.name: Libolo
polities.note: Mbundu kingdom south of the middle Kwanza, east of Kisama; source of Imbangala alliances; under Portuguese influence 18th-19th c.

polities.name: Dembos (Ndembu chiefdoms)
polities.note: Cluster of Mbundu/Kongo chiefdoms in the hills between Kongo and Ndongo (including Mbwila of the 1665 battle); nominal vassals of Kongo then Portugal; finally conquered in the Dembos campaigns 1907-1919.

polities.name: Portuguese Angola
polities.note: Colony founded at Luanda 1575 with Benguela from 1617; effective control limited to Luanda-Kwanza corridor (Massangano, Ambaca, Pungo Andongo), Benguela coast and Caconda until the late 19th c.; Moçâmedes 1840; Huíla plateau 1850s-80s; full interior conquest 1890-1920.

polities.name: Portuguese São Tomé and Príncipe
polities.note: Portuguese plantation colony settled from 1485/1493; Dutch occupation 1641-1648; seat moved to Santo António (Príncipe) 1753-1852.

polities.name: Angolares
polities.note: Maroon community in the forested south of São Tomé, with its own king; raided Portuguese plantations (notably 1574, and with Amador's revolt 1595); submitted to Portugal by treaty c.1693 but kept autonomy.

polities.name: Yaka Kingdom
polities.note: Lunda-founded kingdom (Kiamfu) on the middle Kwango ruling Yaka and Suku populations; paid tribute to the Mwant Yav; resisted Congo Free State until 1906.

polities.name: Suku Kingdom
polities.note: Kingdom of the Meni Kongo east of the Yaka between the Wamba and Inzia rivers; rival of Yaka; subdued by Congo Free State c.1906.

polities.name: Bailundo
polities.note: Largest Ovimbundu kingdom on the Benguela highlands; caravan-trade power in the 19th c.; Portuguese fort 1896; Bailundo revolt 1902 crushed 1903.

polities.name: Bié
polities.note: Eastern Ovimbundu kingdom on the Kwanza headwaters, base of long-distance caravans (Silva Porto); conquered by Portugal 1890 after Ndunduma's war. Worldstatesmen dates ruler list from 1795.

polities.name: Wambu
polities.note: Central Ovimbundu kingdom; extinguished by Portugal 1902.

polities.name: Ciyaka
polities.note: Southwestern Ovimbundu kingdom between Wambu and Kalukembe; ruler list from c.1810; under Portuguese rule after 1903 (kingship continued to 1940).

polities.name: Ngalangi
polities.note: Southern Ovimbundu kingdom on the upper Kunene/Kubango divide.

polities.name: Ndulu
polities.note: Northern Ovimbundu kingdom, often tributary to Bailundo or Bié.

polities.name: Kalukembe
polities.note: Southwestern Ovimbundu kingdom near the Portuguese presidio of Caconda.

polities.name: Cingolo
polities.note: Minor Ovimbundu kingdom between Bailundo, Wambu and Bié.

polities.name: Sambu
polities.note: Minor Ovimbundu kingdom south-east of Wambu.

polities.name: Humbe
polities.note: Nkhumbi kingdom on the middle Kunene; Portuguese fort 1859, revolts, final conquest 1898.

polities.name: Mulondo
polities.note: Nyaneka-Nkhumbi kingdom on the Kunene above Humbe.

polities.name: Huíla
polities.note: Nyaneka (Mwila) kingdom of the Huíla plateau; Portuguese post 1769, colonised from the 1850s (Boer settlers at Humpata 1881).

polities.name: Ombandja
polities.note: Ovambo kingdom west of Evale between the Kunene and Kwanyama; defeated by Portugal 1904-1907.

polities.name: Evale
polities.note: Northernmost Ovambo kingdom on the Cuvelai; occupied by Portugal 1907.

polities.name: Uukwanyama
polities.note: Largest Ovambo kingdom straddling the modern Angola-Namibia border on the Cuvelai floodplain; last independent king Mandume ya Ndemufayo fought Portugal (1915) and died fighting South Africa 1917.

polities.name: Ondonga
polities.note: Southeasternmost Ovambo kingdom reaching toward Etosha; Finnish mission at Olukonda 1870; under German then South African protection (South African rule 1915); kingship continues.

polities.name: Uukwambi
polities.note: Ovambo kingdom west of Ondonga; king Iipumbu deposed by South Africa 1932.

polities.name: Ongandjera
polities.note: Western Ovambo kingdom.

polities.name: Uukwaluudhi
polities.note: Western Ovambo kingdom.

polities.name: Ombalantu
polities.note: Western Ovambo group which abolished its kingship (traditionally in the 18th/early 19th c.) and was ruled by a council of headmen.

polities.name: Kwangali
polities.note: Westernmost Kavango kingdom on the Okavango river (both banks, Angola/Namibia); German protection from 1909-1910.

polities.name: Mbukushu
polities.note: Kavango kingdom on the Okavango around the Popa falls and Andara; rainmaker kings; paid tribute to the Lozi in the 19th c.

polities.name: Mbunda Kingdom
polities.note: Mbunda kingdom in southeastern Angola (Moxico/Cuando Cubango); part of the population migrated to Barotseland c.1800; Portuguese conquest 1914 (death of Mwene Mbandu Kapova).

polities.name: Luvale
polities.note: Lunda-derived chiefdoms (senior title Ndungu, also Kakenge) on the upper Zambezi in eastern Moxico and northwestern Zambia; slave-raiding traders in the 19th c.; partitioned Portugal/Britain 1905.

polities.name: Chokwe chiefdoms
polities.note: Decentralised chiefdoms under Lunda-derived titles (Mwa Chisenge, Ndumba Tembo) at the headwaters of the Kwango, Kasai and Kwanza; from the 1850s Chokwe hunters and traders expanded north, sacking the Lunda capital 1887; checked by Lunda/Congo Free State and Portugal c.1898-1900.

polities.name: Barotseland
polities.note: Luyi/Lozi kingdom of the upper Zambezi floodplain under the Litunga; expanded under Mulambwa (c.1780-1830) over Nkoya, Mbunda, Toka, Subiya, Mbukushu; overrun by the Kololo 1838/1840-1864; restored 1864; Lewanika's BSAC concessions 1890/1900, protectorate within Northern Rhodesia.

polities.name: Kololo Kingdom
polities.note: Sotho-speaking Kololo under Sebetwane conquered Barotseland c.1838-1840 and ruled from Linyanti (Chobe) and Naliele; collapsed in a Lozi rising 1864.

polities.name: Mutondo (Nkoya)
polities.note: Senior Nkoya kingship east of the Barotse floodplain on the Kafue-Luena watershed; tributary to the Lozi from the early 19th c.

polities.name: Kahare (Nkoya)
polities.note: Nkoya/Mashasha chieftainship south of Mutondo toward the Kafue; Lozi tributary.

polities.name: Kasempa (Kaonde)
polities.note: Kaonde chiefdoms between the upper Kafue and Lunga; Kasempa (Jipumpu) became paramount in the later 19th c. raiding neighbours; BSAC administration from 1901.

polities.name: Kanongesha (Ndembu Lunda)
polities.note: Senior Ndembu (southern Lunda) title on the Zambezi-Kasai watershed (Mwinilunga), founded by Lunda emigrants; nominal tribute to the Mwant Yav.

polities.name: Ishinde (Lunda)
polities.note: Southern Lunda chiefdom on the upper Zambezi east bank; Lozi pressure in the 19th c.

polities.name: Lunda Empire
polities.note: Ruund kingship on the Kalanyi/Mbuji-Mayi headwaters; Mwant Yav title consolidated c.1665 (Yav a Nawej); tribute zone at height (c.1750-1850) from the Kwango to the Luapula via Kazembe; Musumba sacked by the Chokwe 1887; Congo Free State/Portuguese partition 1890s. Capital (Musumba) moved with each reign around the Kalanyi valley.

polities.name: Luba Empire
polities.note: Luba kingship centred on the Upemba depression and Lomami-Lualaba interfluve; expanded greatly under Ilunga Sungu, Kumwimba Ngombe and Ilunga Kabale (c.1780-1870) to Lake Tanganyika and the Lomami; succession war after 1870s, Yeke and Swahili raids; split into two lineages 1889; Congo Free State.

polities.name: Kanyok Kingdom
polities.note: Luba-speaking kingdom on the upper Lubilash/Mbuji-Mayi between Luba and Lunda; threw off Kalundwe tribute in the early 18th c. and raided Lunda; under Congo Free State from the 1890s.

polities.name: Kalundwe
polities.note: Luba-related kingdom west of the Luba heartland between the Lubilash and the Lomami; held tribute over Kanyok until the early 18th c.; generally within the Luba orbit.

polities.name: Kazembe
polities.note: Eastern Lunda kingdom founded by Lunda generals who settled on the Luapula c.1740-1750; controlled copper and the trade to Tete/Zanzibar; lost lands west of the Luapula to Msiri's Yeke after 1856; BSAC occupied 1899, kingdom continues in Zambia.

polities.name: Yeke Kingdom
polities.note: Founded by the Nyamwezi trader Msiri in Katanga, taking the western provinces of Kazembe and Luba borderlands; controlled copper and the ivory/slave trade; Msiri killed by the Stairs expedition Dec 1891, Congo Free State took over.

polities.name: Musokantanda (Lunda)
polities.note: Lunda (Ruund) satellite chiefdom on the upper Lualaba-Lufira watershed (modern Kolwezi-Mutshatsha); pressed by Yeke after 1856.

polities.name: Kuba Kingdom
polities.note: Bushong-led federation founded by Shyaam a-Mbul c.1625 between the Sankuru, Kasai and Lulua; conquered by Congo Free State forces 1899-1900, kingship continues.

polities.name: Luluwa (Kalamba Mukenge)
polities.note: Luluwa paramountcy built by Kalamba Mukenge on the ivory/rubber trade with Chokwe and Ovimbundu caravans; allied with Wissmann's Luluabourg station (1884); absorbed by Congo Free State by the late 1890s.

polities.name: Songye chiefdoms
polities.note: Fortified town-chiefdoms (Kalebwe, Eki, Bena Kibeshi) between the Sankuru and Lomami north of Luba; raided by Swahili-Arab and Tetela forces (Ngongo Leteta) in the 1880s.

polities.name: Pende chiefdoms
polities.note: Pende chiefdoms on the Kwilu and Loange after migration from the Angolan Kwango in the 17th c.; under Lunda/Chokwe pressure.

polities.name: Bobangi trading towns
polities.note: Riverine Bobangi trading towns controlling canoe trade on the Congo and lower Ubangi between Pool Malebo and the equator; no single ruler; superseded by Congo Free State steamers.

polities.name: Tippu Tip's Manyema state
polities.note: Swahili-Arab trading and raiding state in Manyema around Kasongo and Nyangwe built by Tippu Tip; he was CFS governor of Stanley Falls 1887-1890; destroyed in the Congo Arab war 1892-1894.

polities.name: Nsama (Tabwa)
polities.note: Tabwa paramountcy between Lake Mweru and Lake Tanganyika; Nsama Chipili defeated by Tippu Tip 1867; fragmented thereafter.

polities.name: Kabare (Bushi)
polities.note: Principal Shi kingdom (Mwami Kabare) west of Lake Kivu; rival of Ngweshe and Rwanda; Congo Free State posts from 1900.

polities.name: Ngweshe (Bushi)
polities.note: Southern Shi kingdom southwest of Lake Kivu.

polities.name: Havu Kingdom (Idjwi)
polities.note: Havu kingdom on Idjwi island and the western Kivu shore; often contested with Rwanda.

polities.name: Mangbetu Kingdom
polities.note: Mabiti-clan elites unified Mangbetu clans in the late 18th c.; Nabiembali extended rule over Bangba, Mayogo, Barambo etc. on the Uele and its southern tributaries; he was killed 1859 by his sons; Munza (visited by Schweinfurth 1870) killed 1873, after which the kingdom split into rival branches (Niangara, Yangala, Mbunza) under Egyptian/Sudanese pressure; Congo Free State 1892.

polities.name: Mangbetu successor kingdoms
polities.note: Rival Mangbetu branches after Munza's death; Niangara's branch separate 1873-1895; Egyptian Equatoria influence 1870s-1883, Congo Free State from 1892.

polities.name: Gbudwe's Zande kingdom
polities.note: Avungara Zande kingdom of Gbudwe (r. 1870-1905) on the Nile-Congo watershed (Western Equatoria, extending into Uele); Gbudwe killed resisting a British patrol 1905.

polities.name: Tambura's Zande kingdom
polities.note: Northwestern Avungara Zande kingdom on the upper Mbomu-Sue watershed; came to terms with the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan.

polities.name: Ndoruma's Zande kingdom
polities.note: Avungara Zande king between the Mbomu and the Uele; fought Egyptian-backed traders in the 1870s-80s; under Congo Free State by the mid-1890s. Location approximate.

polities.name: Wando's Zande kingdom
polities.note: Avungara Zande kingdom of Wando and his sons (Ukwe, Renzi, Mbitima) south of the Nile-Congo divide on the upper Uele; Congo Free State posts at Dungu from 1890s. Location approximate.

polities.name: Bakangai's Zande kingdom
polities.note: Avungara Zande kingdom south of the Uele near the Bomokandi; Congo Free State from 1890s. Location approximate.

polities.name: Congo Free State
polities.note: Personal state of Leopold II recognised 1885; effective occupation spread from the river network 1885-1900 (Katanga 1891-92, Arab war 1892-94, Kwango 1890s, Uele 1890s); annexed by Belgium 1908.

polities.name: Bamum Kingdom
polities.note: Founded by Nchare Yen 1394; expanded greatly under Mbuembue (early 19th c.) between the Mbam and Noun rivers; Sultan Njoya (r. 1887-1933) accepted German protection 1902; French administration dismantled royal power 1923-1931.

polities.name: Nso Kingdom
polities.note: Tikar-derived kingdom founded by Ngonnso (14th c.); largest Grassfields fondom on the Bui plateau; fought Bamum; German conquest 1906.

polities.name: Kom Kingdom
polities.note: Grassfields kingdom north of Bamenda (Boyo), established c.1755; German protectorate 1900-1904.

polities.name: Bafut
polities.note: Tikar-derived fondom north of Bamenda; resisted the Germans in the Bafut wars 1901-1907.

polities.name: Bali-Nyonga
polities.note: Chamba (Bali) warrior state that settled south of Bamenda c.1835 after raiding south from the Adamawa; German ally from 1889 (Zintgraff), favoured sub-imperial power over neighbours.

polities.name: Mankon
polities.note: Grassfields fondom (Bamenda); fought Zintgraff's expedition 1891.

polities.name: Bandjoun
polities.note: One of the largest Bamileke chiefdoms; Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916.

polities.name: Bafoussam
polities.note: Bafoussam chiefdom; frequently at war with Bamum to the east. Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916, chiefdom continues.

polities.name: Bangangté
polities.note: Medumba-speaking southern Bamileke chiefdom on the Ndé plateau. Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916, chiefdom continues.

polities.name: Baham
polities.note: Central Bamileke chiefdom. Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916, chiefdom continues.

polities.name: Foréké-Dschang
polities.note: Western Bamileke chiefdom on the Menoua plateau. Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916, chiefdom continues.

polities.name: Bana
polities.note: Southern Bamileke chiefdom (Haut-Nkam). Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916, chiefdom continues.

polities.name: Bafang
polities.note: Southwestern Bamileke chiefdom (Haut-Nkam). Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916, chiefdom continues.

polities.name: Batcham
polities.note: Northern Bamileke chiefdom (Bamboutos). Bamileke chiefdom (fondom) of the western Grassfields; German control c.1900-1916, chiefdom continues.

polities.name: Tikar Kingdom of Bankim
polities.note: Senior Tikar kingdom on the upper Mbam plain, ancestral to Bamum and Nso royal lines; raided by Fulbe (Banyo, Tibati) in the 19th c.

polities.name: Nditam
polities.note: Southern Tikar kingdom on the Mbam.

polities.name: Ngambe-Tikar
polities.note: Tikar kingdom between Bankim and Nditam.

polities.name: Bell (Duala)
polities.note: Senior Duala trading chieftaincy on the Wouri estuary; King Bell and King Akwa signed the German protectorate treaty 12 July 1884.

polities.name: Akwa (Duala)
polities.note: Rival Duala trading chieftaincy (Bonaku/Akwa town, with Deido offshoot 1794) on the Wouri; signed the 1884 German treaty.

polities.name: Bimbia
polities.note: Isubu trading kingdom south of Mount Cameroon; King William I signed anti-slave-trade treaties with Britain 1844-1855 and sold land for Victoria 1858; annexed to German Kamerun 1884.

polities.name: Buea (Bakweri)
polities.note: Bakweri chiefdoms on the slopes of Mount Cameroon; Kuva Likenye defeated a German column 1891, conquered 1894.

polities.name: Basaa
polities.note: Segmentary Basaa lineages between the lower Sanaga and the Nyong without a central ruler; German conquest 1890s.

polities.name: Ewondo (Beti)
polities.note: Beti-Pahuin clans who crossed the Sanaga in the 18th c. and settled around Yaoundé between the Sanaga and Nyong; Germans founded Jaunde station 1889 and installed Atangana as paramount chief.

polities.name: Bulu
polities.note: Beti-Pahuin clans between the Nyong and the Ntem; controlled the hinterland rubber/ivory trade to Kribi; rising against Germany 1899-1901.

polities.name: Fang
polities.note: Fang clans migrating south-west from southern Cameroon through the Woleu-Ntem and Rio Muni toward the Gabon estuary and the Ogooué in the 18th-19th c.; no central ruler; divided between France, Germany and Spain 1885-1900.

polities.name: Maka
polities.note: Segmentary Maka clans of the upper Nyong forest; conquered by Germany 1905-1910.

polities.name: Gbaya
polities.note: Gbaya clans of the savanna of eastern Cameroon and western CAR (Bertoua to Bouar/Carnot); partly tributary to Fulbe Ngaoundéré in the 19th c.; Kongo-Wara rising 1928.

polities.name: Vute chiefdoms
polities.note: Vute chiefdoms on the Sanaga-Mbam (Ngila of Linté, Ngutte) that raided for slaves and ivory under Fulbe influence; conquered by Germany 1899.

polities.name: Ngaoundéré Lamidate
polities.note: Fulbe lamidate on the Adamawa plateau founded c.1835 under the Adamawa (Yola) emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate; raided Gbaya and Mbum; German occupation 1901.

polities.name: Tibati Lamidate
polities.note: Fulbe lamidate on the southern Adamawa plateau (founding traditions c.1808-1830); vassal of Yola; German conquest 1899.

polities.name: Banyo Lamidate
polities.note: Fulbe lamidate on the western Adamawa plateau above the Tikar plain; vassal of Yola; German occupation 1902.

polities.name: German Kamerun
polities.note: German protectorate from the Duala treaty of 12 July 1884; capital Buea 1901-1909; inland conquest 1889-1907 (Yaoundé 1889, Bafut 1907, Adamawa 1901-02); expanded by Neukamerun 1911; conquered by Allies 1914-1916.

polities.name: Kingdom of Orungu
polities.note: Myene-speaking kingdom on the Cape Lopez peninsula and lower Ogooué delta; slaving port at Sangatanga; commercial influence up the Ogooué and to Fernan Vaz; French cession treaty 1862; monarchy abolished 1927.

polities.name: Mpongwe chiefdoms
polities.note: Myene-speaking Mpongwe clan chiefdoms around the Gabon (Komo) estuary trading with Europeans; King Denis ceded land to France 1839, King Louis 1842 (Fort d'Aumale/Libreville 1843); absorbed into French Gabon.

polities.name: Nkomi
polities.note: Myene-speaking Nkomi chieftaincy around Fernan Vaz lagoon south of Orungu; French treaties 1860s; absorbed into French Gabon.

polities.name: Galoa
polities.note: Myene-speaking Galoa chieftaincies on the middle Ogooué lakes around Lambaréné; trade intermediaries; French posts from 1870s.

polities.name: Benga (Cabo San Juan / Corisco)
polities.note: Benga kingship at Cabo San Juan (Rio Muni coast) with seat moved to Corisco c.1840; split 1858; Corisco line extinguished 1910 under Spain.

polities.name: Bubi of Bioko
polities.note: Bubi clans of Bioko united under a paramount (Moka, from c.1840s; Malabo Lopelo Melaka 1899-1904) based in the southern highlands; Spanish control of the interior from 1904.

polities.name: Spanish Guinea
polities.note: Bioko and Annobón ceded by Portugal 1778 (Treaty of El Pardo); British naval base at Clarence 1827-1843; effective Spanish rule from 1843/1858, coastal Bioko and Corisco; Rio Muni recognised 1900. The 1900-1968 phase extent is the mainland Rio Muni block only (seat stays on Bioko, whose outline is the main extent); Corisco/Elobey/Annobón islets omitted.

polities.name: French Gabon and Congo
polities.note: French Gabon estuary posts from the 1839/1842 treaties (Libreville 1849); Ogooué exploration 1870s; de Brazza's Tio treaty 1880 and Brazzaville; French Congo constituted 1882-1891, including Ubangi-Shari from 1894; capital moved to Brazzaville 1904; became French Equatorial Africa 1910.

polities.name: Kingdom of Baguirmi
polities.note: Barma kingdom on the lower Chari southeast of Lake Chad (traditional founding 1522; alternative 1480s); tributary of Bornu from Idris Alooma's time to c.1750; expanded under Burkumanda (1635-1665) to Lake Chad and along the Chari; conquered by Wadai 1805 (tributary thereafter, sacked 1870); burned by Rabih 1893; French protectorate 1897.

polities.name: Wadai Sultanate
polities.note: Maba sultanate founded by Abd al-Karim overthrowing the Tunjur (1635); capital Wara, moved to Abéché under Sharif (r. 1835-1858); conquered Bagirmi 1805 and extended rule to Dar Sila, Dar Runga, Salamat and (late 19th c.) Dar al-Kuti, Kanem and Borku; French took Abéché 1909, conquest complete 1912.

polities.name: Tunjur Kingdom (Wadai)
polities.note: Tunjur dynasty ruling the Wadai highlands (and earlier Darfur) from roughly the 15th c. until overthrown by Abd al-Karim in 1635; seat location approximate.

polities.name: Bulala Sultanate
polities.note: Bulala captured Kanem from the Sayfawa in the late 14th c. (Njimi taken); Idris Katagarmabe retook Kanem c.1507 and the Bulala governed it as a Bornu province, rebelling until Idris Alooma; driven from Kanem by Wadai c.1630; small sultanate at Yao by Lake Fitri until French occupation May 1909.

polities.name: Kanem (Alifate of Mao)
polities.note: After the Bulala were driven out, Kanem was governed by the Dalatoa line of alifas at Mao as vassals of Bornu, later of Wadai; under heavy Awlad Sulayman and Tuareg pressure in the 19th c.; French occupation c.1900-1903.

polities.name: Dar Sila
polities.note: Daju sultanate in southeastern Chad tracing its dynasty to Daju rule in Darfur; brought under Wadai influence by Muhammad Sabun (early 19th c.); last independent sultanate conquered by France 1916. Founding date approximate.

polities.name: Dar Tama
polities.note: Tama sultanate in the hills between Wadai and Darfur, contested tributary of both; French occupation c.1910. Founding date approximate.

polities.name: Dar Runga
polities.note: Runga sultanate south of Wadai in the Aouk/Salamat border zone; Wadai tributary; Dar al-Kuti was its frontier dependency from c.1830; conquered by Rabih 1890 and merged into Dar al-Kuti. Founding date and seat approximate.

polities.name: Dar al-Kuti
polities.note: Frontier slave-raiding state founded c.1830 under Dar Runga/Wadai; Rabih installed Muhammad al-Sanussi 1890, who built a fortified capital at N'Délé (1894) and raided across central CAR; French protectorate 1897; Sanussi killed 1911, Ouanda Djallé fell Dec 1912.

polities.name: Rabih az-Zubayr's state
polities.note: Sudanese warlord's slave-raiding state: operated from the Banda/Kreish country and Dar al-Kuti (1879-1890), conquered Dar Runga and Bagirmi (1890-1893), took Bornu and ruled from Dikwa 1893-1900; killed by the French at Kousseri 22 April 1900. Probably also listed by the West Africa (Bornu) gazetteer.

polities.name: Kenga
polities.note: Kenga chiefdom of the Guéra hills (Hadjerai), tributary of Bagirmi and raided by Wadai; tradition makes it the origin of the Bagirmi dynasty. Dates approximate.

polities.name: Léré (Moundang)
polities.note: Moundang kingdom under the Gong of Léré in southwestern Chad, resisting Fulbe raids from Adamawa; French from 1900s.

polities.name: Logone-Birni
polities.note: Walled Kotoko city-kingdom (town traditionally founded c.1700 by Prince Bruha per Wikipedia; Lagwan polity older) on the Logone south of Lake Chad, tributary of Bornu (and at times Bagirmi); sultanate title from 1805; occupied by Rabih 1893, then partitioned. Probably also covered by the West Africa/Bornu gazetteer.

polities.name: Sara chiefdoms
polities.note: Sara peoples of the Chari-Logone valleys of southern Chad, organised in lineage villages with ritual chiefs (Mbang of Bédaya); targeted by Bagirmi, Wadai and Dar al-Kuti slave raids.

polities.name: Banda
polities.note: Banda clans of central CAR (Ouaka, Kotto, Haute-Kotto), decentralised and heavily raided by Dar al-Kuti, Rabih and Zande/Bandia states in the 19th c.

polities.name: Bangassou Sultanate
polities.note: Bandia-ruled Nzakara kingdom on the Mbomu (sultanate c.1876); Congo Free State protectorate 1890-1894, French suzerainty 1894, protectorate 1909, suppressed 1917.

polities.name: Rafai Sultanate
polities.note: Bandia-Zande kingdom on the middle Mbomu (sultanate c.1875); Congo Free State protectorate 1892-1909, French protectorate 1909, suppressed 1939.

polities.name: Zemio Sultanate
polities.note: Avungara Zande kingdom on the upper Mbomu (sultanate c.1872); Congo Free State protectorate 1894-1909, French protectorate 1909, suppressed 1923.

gaps.area: Central Congo basin rainforest (Cuvette centrale: Tshuapa, Lomami, Lulonga, Lopori, Ikelemba, Maringa basins; Mongo, Ekonda, Ngombe, Lokele, Topoke, Mbole peoples)
gaps.note: Densely forested and inhabited by village- and lineage-level societies without kingdoms (Mongo big-men, Ekonda/Nkundo chiefs). Not empty land but no polity with a recognised seat; Congo Free State posts from 1883-1895.

gaps.area: Ituri forest and northeastern Congo (Lese, Mbuti, Bira, Budu, Mamvu)
gaps.note: Forest foragers and segmentary farming societies; partial Mangbetu and Zande influence on the northern fringe; Swahili-Arab raiding 1880s; Congo Free State late 1890s.

gaps.area: Interior Gabon and Congo-Brazzaville forests (Nzebi, Punu, Eshira, Kota, Mbede/Obamba, Kwele, Mbochi, Makaa, Bakota; Chaillu and Du Chaillu massifs, Sangha-Likouala)
gaps.note: Clan and village chiefdoms without large states; Punu and Eshira chiefs traded with the coast; Mbochi/Likouala riverine chiefs. Could be filled as low-confidence tribal nations; French occupation 1880s-1900s.

gaps.area: Southeastern Cameroon and southwestern CAR forest (Dja, Boumba, Sangha headwaters; Baka foragers, Kako, Mpiemu, Bangando)
gaps.note: Sparse forest population without polities; Gbaya and Maka edges itemised.

gaps.area: Northeastern CAR and Chad-Sudan borderlands (Dar Fertit: Kreish, Gula, Yulu, Sara Kaba; Vakaga, Bamingui)
gaps.note: Small-scale societies repeatedly depopulated by slave raids from Darfur, Wadai, Zubayr's Bahr al-Ghazal and Dar al-Kuti; nominal tribute zones of Dar Runga/Wadai.

gaps.area: Southern Chad central plain (Salamat, Guéra outside Kenga, Mayo-Kebbi Massa/Musgum, Tupuri, Nielim, Bua)
gaps.note: Small chiefdoms (Niellim, Bua, Massa, Musgum) tributary to Bagirmi or Wadai; Salamat was a Wadai province. Partly covered by Bagirmi/Wadai extents.

gaps.area: Angolan southeast and Kalahari fringe (Cuando-Cubango east of the Kavango kingdoms: Luchazi, Nyemba, Nganguela, !Kung San)
gaps.note: Thinly settled; Nganguela/Luchazi village chiefs and San foragers; Lozi and Mbunda tribute reached parts.

gaps.area: Namib/Kaokoveld edge of southwestern Angola (Moçâmedes desert, Kuvale/Herero, Himba)
gaps.note: Pastoral Kuvale and Herero groups without states; Portuguese Moçâmedes from 1840. Herero/Himba south of the Kunene belong to the southern Africa gazetteer.

gaps.area: Southern Zambia and Kafue (Tonga, Ila, Lenje, Toka-Leya, Subiya)
gaps.note: Mostly acephalous Tonga/Ila societies; Subiya and Toka paid tribute to Barotseland. Bemba, Ngoni and eastern Zambia kingdoms are outside this region (East/Southern Africa gazetteer).

gaps.area: Lower Kasai-Kwilu between Pende, Yaka and Kuba (Mbala, Mbun, Dinga, Lele, Wongo, Sakata, Yansi)
gaps.note: Small chiefdoms; partly within the uncertain Mwene Muji sphere (to c.1640) and later the Boma/Lunda/Kuba margins.

gaps.area: Southern savanna before c.1600 (Katanga/Upemba, Lunda plateau, upper Zambezi, Benguela highlands, Kwango)
gaps.note: Precursor polities are known only from oral tradition and archaeology (Kongolo's Luba state before 1585, Ruund chiefdoms before the Mwant Yav, Luyana before the Litunga, pre-Ovimbundu highland chiefdoms). Extents for 1400-1600 here are guesswork; the atlas may leave these areas blank or use low-confidence Luba/Lunda core polygons.

gaps.area: Cameroon western Grassfields and Bamileke plateau
gaps.note: Not empty: about 100 Bamileke chiefdoms and dozens of Grassfields fondoms (Bambui, Bambalang, Babungo, Oku, Ndu, Bum, Aghem, Batibo, Mbot, Nkar...) existed; only the largest are itemised, each with a small reach_km. worldstatesmen Cameroon_native lists many more.

gaps.area: Cross River / Manyu and Mamfe forest (Ejagham, Banyang, Bakossi, Balong) in southwestern Cameroon
gaps.note: Village-group and clan chiefdoms without large states; Ekpe/Ngbe society authority. Bakossi and Balong paramountcies are later colonial-era creations.
